issues.failure_explanation: The 'if' direction asserts that existence of $\partial^{\sd}_v f(x)$ forces $\partial^{\pm}_v f(x)$ to exist. Counterexample ($X=Y=\mathbb{R}$, $x=0$, $v=1$): let $f(0)=0$, $f(t)=t\,p(t)$ and $f(-t)=-t(1-p(t))$ for $t>0$, where $p(t)\in\{0,1\}$ oscillates without a limit (e.g. $p(t)=1$ iff $\sin(1/t)\ge0$). Then $\arctan p+\arctan(1-p)=\pi/4$ for every $t$, so the specular quotient in \eqref{eq:spG} is identically $\tan(\pi/8)=\sqrt2-1$ and $\partial^{\sd}_1 f(0)$ exists, while $\partial^{\pm}_1 f(0)$ oscillate between 0 and 1 and do not exist, contradicting (H1). The proof of the converse is also invalid: from a two-sided bound on $\arctan((f(x+hv)-f(x))/(h\|v\|))+\arctan((f(x)-f(x-hv))/(h\|v\|))$ it infers the bounds on the forward quotient via monotonicity of $\tan$ across the branch discontinuity at $\pm\pi/2$; e.g. for smooth $f$ with $\partial^{\sd}_v f(x)=c>0$ the derived upper bound $\|v\|\tan(2\arctan((c+h)/\|v\|)+\pi/2)$ is negative while the forward quotient tends to $c>0$.

issues.failure_explanation:
The method is defined (and its convergence proved) under this condition, presented as a property of the construction with $\xi_k$ ranging over the component indices. But specular gradients are nonlinear in the objective: the average of component specular gradients is not the specular gradient of the average. Counterexample ($n=1$, $m=2$, uniform $\xi$): $f_1=10\max(x,0)$, $f_2\equiv0$ (both convex and specularly Fr'echet differentiable), $f= rac12(f_1+f_2)=5\max(x,0)$; then $
abla^s f_1(0)=	an( rac12\arctan 10)\approx0.904$, $
abla^s f_2(0)=0$, while $
abla^s f(0)=	an( rac12\arctan 5)\approx0.814
eq rac12(0.904+0)$. Hence the pseudocode's estimator is biased, the defining condition is generally unsatisfiable (including at the $\ell^1$-kinks of the paper's Elastic-Net experiments), and the convergence theorem, whose proof uses the condition, does not apply to the implemented method.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum one must either restrict to instances where $\frac1m\sum_j\nabla^s f_j(\mathbf{x})=\nabla^s f(\mathbf{x})$ (excluding the nonsmooth cases of interest) or develop a convergence analysis for the biased stochastic specular gradient.
issues.overall_effect: The defining invariant of S-SPEG (and of H-SPEG, which switches to it) fails in general, so the stochastic convergence theorem guarantees nothing for the algorithm as pseudocoded.
issues.title: S-SPEG's unbiasedness condition $\mathbb{E}[\nabla^s f_{\xi_k}|\mathbf{x}_k]=\nabla^s f(\mathbf{x}_k)$ fails for component sampling
issues.why_classification: The method's core premise is mathematically false in general; no supported resolution preserves the advertised convergence guarantee for the implemented method without essentially new analysis.
